rows_detail.current: background verification proportionate to the role
rows_detail.proposed: Background checks sized to what the role can actually reach, rather than applied uniformly. The same check on everyone is both wasteful and insufficient, which is why proportionality is the requirement and thoroughness is not.

rows_detail.current: security responsibilities expressed in employment terms
rows_detail.proposed: Security duties written into the employment contract, where they outlast the induction session everyone forgets. It is also what makes a disciplinary process defensible: the obligation was agreed, not announced.

rows_detail.current: ensuring people know their security responsibilities
rows_detail.proposed: Three different things inside one control: knowing a rule exists, understanding why it exists, and being able to act on it. A programme that only announces policy has done the first and neither of the others.

rows_detail.current: the process following a security policy violation
rows_detail.proposed: The defined response to a violation, which has to exist before one happens. Its working purpose is consistency: inventing a response case by case is how two similar breaches end up with different outcomes.

rows_detail.current: the underlying reason a nonconformity occurred
rows_detail.proposed: Why the failure was possible, not what failed. Stopping at the immediate cause buys a fix that holds until the same conditions recur, which is exactly the difference between correction and corrective action.

rows_detail.current: judging whether controls achieve their intended outcome
rows_detail.proposed: Asking whether a control is doing its job, not whether it is there. A control can be fully implemented, documented and audited and still not move the risk it was selected to treat.

rows_detail.current: unsanctioned AI tooling adopted outside the approval process
rows_detail.proposed: AI tools brought in without going through approval, usually by people trying to work faster rather than to evade anything. Treating it as misconduct pushes it further out of sight, which is the opposite of what an inventory needs.

rows_detail.current: the interval between compromise and detection, and why it widens here
rows_detail.proposed: The interval between compromise and detection. It widens around AI tooling because the activity often produces no conventional log entry, so monitoring has nothing to notice in the first place.
rows_detail.note: The current text ends 'and why it widens here' and never says why - a pointer with no antecedent, the defect class from batch 1. The replacement answers it.

rows_detail.current: activity that generates no conventional log entry
rows_detail.proposed: Activity that leaves no trace in the logs anyone is watching. Detection needs a signal to exist before it can be missed, which is what makes this a property of the estate rather than of the monitoring.

rows_detail.current: tooling adopted individually and never recorded
rows_detail.proposed: Tooling taken up one person at a time and recorded nowhere. Each decision is small enough to look like nobody's business, which is how an estate acquires exposure that no asset register can show.

rows_detail.current: how a written provision becomes a daily decision
rows_detail.proposed: The distance between a written provision and what someone actually does at the keyboard. A rule demanding a judgement nobody has been equipped to make is unenforceable in practice, whatever it says on paper.
rows_detail.note: The current text is a how-frame with no answer - the same pointer-with-no-antecedent shape.
